caption:
Some people say theek hai like they are giving up.

And some say it like they have already packed a small bag and moved into your tiny universe.

Send this to your jo tu kahegi wahi hoga person.
alt_text: Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 1: Warm full-scene @a.storyof.two illustration. Aachu is mid-decision in an ordinary Indian public-life moment, laughing with shy dramatic energy and one hand near her face. Zuv stands close beside her with dark wavy hair, beard, thick brows, and an amused calm smile, already adjusting the plan on his phone with willing theek-hai energy. Their body language is the whole visual proof. Line: Me with my "jo tu kahegi wahi hoga"

Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 2: Soft storybook scene on an Indian street or inside a parked car: Aachu points toward a sudden new plan with sparkling certainty while Zuv calmly changes the route on his phone, already smiling. Tiny route arrows and checkmarks can float as hand-drawn scene doodles, but the main image remains their faces, hands, and shared joke. Line: In another universe, he still changes the plan.

Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 3: Full illustrated everyday scene: they are almost about to argue, Aachu mock-annoyed and expressive, while Zuv steps in with water, keys, charger, or a small snack and a calm smile that softens the timing. A tiny handwritten status note may sit near them, integrated into the scene. No app UI, no calendar screen. Line: Argument status: rescheduled.

Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 4: Scene-first illustration: Aachu explains her logic with mock-serious confidence while Zuv looks at the phone, weather, menu, or route proof and realizes she was right. He adds his own amused checkmark gesture, smiling like he is in on the bit. The joke is mutual and affectionate, never a boss-wife setup. Line: Terms & conditions: she is probably right.

Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 5: Tender full-scene visual: Zuv voluntarily steps into Aachu’s lively little world of plans, moods, route arrows, tiny hearts, and playful notes. Aachu is inviting him in, not commanding him. His body leans forward with a warm smile so the viewer reads choice, delight, and participation. Line: Not because he lost. Because he likes her world.

Soft hand-drawn @a.storyof.two illustrated scene 6: Ordinary Indian couple moment in the accepted storybook style: Zuv offers theek-hai through action, maybe holding her bag, phone, water, keys, or changed plan with an amused soft smile. Aachu beams because the phrase has become his private love language. No literal bouquet, no grand romance pose, no label-only composition. Line: Some men bring flowers. Mine brings theek hai.
